mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a UNRATE decrease, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) crosses above 4.5%, it may indicate a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate investments, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day windows after FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is strong and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is low, it indicates a robust economy, which may lead to increased consumer and business spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following strong GDP growth and low UNRATE, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) during a late-cycle expansion indicates strong demand for housing, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following an increase in HOUST, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates increased economic output, which may lead to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following an increase in INDPRO, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 50% of the 5-day windows following significant PAYEMS growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is strong but consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) growth is moderate, it indicates a balanced economy with controlled inflation, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following strong GDP growth with moderate CPI growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) during a monetary easing cycle may lead to increased borrowing and investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a FEDFUNDS decrease, the hypothesis is rejected.
